key_insight: Nd and Ce can segregate to grain boundaries in both bcc Fe and TiN, but TiN largely retains grain-boundary strength while Fe is significantly weakened.
engineering_relevance: This suggests TiN and related nitride coatings may better resist fission-product-assisted corrosion cracking and intergranular fracture in FCCI environments.
method: First-principles segregation calculations for Nd/Ce at six coincident-site lattice grain boundaries in bcc Fe and TiN.
Decohesion and traction-separation simulations to quantify work of separation and ideal crack-opening resistance.
Bonding analysis to identify how segregation alters interfacial chemistry and mechanical response.
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated grain boundaries, Nd/Ce segregation was favorable in both materials, but TiN showed near-unity median work-of-separation retention and much higher retained peak traction than Fe.
watch_item: The conclusions are atomistic and grain-boundary specific, so real coatings may differ due to microstructure, defects, temperature, and radiation effects.
paper_title: Grain boundary strength and corrosion cracking susceptibility in TiN coatings under fission product segregation
